newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up on expected capital inflow.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up on expected capital inflow.

text.p: The won closed stronger versus the dollar on Wednesday on the back of expectations of foreign capital inflow and worries over possible central bank dollar selling, dealers said.
The won closed at 827.60 after opening at 829.50. It fluctuated in a range of 827.30 to 829.60.
Dealers said market talk that a local company would supply $110 million to the interbank market in the near future dampened the dollar buying sentiment.
"The expectation killed the bids," said a trader at a European bank.
Traders expect a upward correction for the local unit on Thursday when the foreign capital inflow is seen materialising.
A range of 825.00 to 827.60 is seen for Thursday with a base mid-rate of 828.00. Today's mid-rate stood at 828.60.
